$note: Single source for every number in spec §5.6 (R5.7). Generated by measuring commit 3176725 (main, tip of Wave 2 — 'docs: Wave 2 gate browser flows recorded') with scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs's own method, then hand-tightened. Fix round on 2026-09-07 (Opus review of c6fef80) re-measured the full built tree — not just the spec's 12 anticipated routes — and found four more app routes the original generation never looked at: /preview, /login, /admin and / (`scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs`'s own reverse check now fails the gate if a fifth ever slips in unnoticed). Do not hand-write a number here without re-running the measurement; the whole point of this gate is that it reflects a real build, not the spec's provisional table.
method: docs/research/v2/codebase-audit.md §3: read each route's .next/server/app/**/page_client-reference-manifest.js, resolve its entryJSFiles list against on-disk .next/static/chunks/*.js sizes, sum uncompressed bytes.
rules: (a) no route's budgetBytes may exceed its v1Bytes, ever, even when the measured tree is currently over budget. scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs enforces this at load time — a budgetBytes above v1Bytes fails the gate before a single route is measured.

(b) every route whose measured size exceeds specTargetBytes (the spec §5.6 direction) carries a named row in `ledger` saying which library is responsible and whether it is split, deferred, or accepted. Enforced: each ledger row now carries a `routes` array, and the gate fails if a route measures over its specTargetBytes without appearing in at least one row's `routes`.

(c) every route the build actually produces must appear either in `routes` (with a real budget) or in `unbudgetedRoutes` (with a stated reason) — scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs diffs the measured tree against both and fails the gate on anything in neither, so a route cannot go silently ungated.

That means both already measure over budget today (415,294 B and 245,723 B respectively, against 346,112 B and 203,776 B ceilings), which is the gate correctly surfacing a real regression rather than hiding it. / is over by roughly 1 KB (72,683 B measured against a 71,680 B v1-equal ceiling) — noise-adjacent, but rule (a) forbids raising the ceiling to hide even a 1 KB regression, so it stays named rather than rounded away.

unbudgetedRoutes.reason: Dev-only Java-adapter certification harness (src/app/preview/layout.tsx calls notFound() outside NODE_ENV === 'development', same gate as /preview itself). The exercise bank it certifies against is injected by e2e/java/*.spec.ts via page.addInitScript, never imported by the page itself, so this route carries no reference-solution weight and never reaches a learner in any deployed build. Measured for the record at 77,641 bytes on 2026-09-07 (well within any plausible budget), but a route this narrowly scoped to one e2e harness does not need a standing production ceiling — it is listed here, by name, with a reason, specifically so it is never silently invisible to the check above.

ledger.library: src/lib/agents/buddy.ts (zod + the DeepSeek agent-request/response schemas), pulled into the client bundle by src/components/buddy/state.ts's plain `import { REFUSAL } from '@/lib/agents/buddy'`
ledger.note: This is not one of the spec's anticipated overages — it is a real bug found by this measurement, present identically on all 13 routes above, including /preview (fix-round finding: /preview renders the same shell and buddy widget as every authenticated route, and its manifest carries the identical 475,150-byte leak chunk `415yhzio7b-ph.js`, confirmed by direct chunk inspection on 2026-09-07). Before the fix, one 475,150-byte chunk carries the leak (confirmed by content: it has zod's `ZodObject`/`ZodString` exports and the literal string "deepseek"); state.ts wants only the REFUSAL string constant, but a non-type-only import of one export from an agent module pulls the whole module — zod included — into every route that renders the buddy widget in the shell (today, every authenticated route plus /preview). Verified directly: patching state.ts in a disposable worktree to hold its own copy of the REFUSAL string instead of importing it, then rebuilding, drops every one of these routes by exactly 375,465 bytes (confirmed identical across all 13 routes) — Turbopack re-packs the remaining ~99,685 bytes of that chunk (the buddy widget's own legitimate code) into a smaller, separate chunk rather than deleting it outright, so 375,465 bytes — not the full 475,150-byte chunk — is the true, fixable cost. Fix: move REFUSAL into a client-safe module with no zod import (or re-export it from a `'use client'`-safe barrel that never imports the agent files), not read from src/lib/agents/buddy.ts on the client. Out of T3.1's ownership (src/components/buddy/** belongs to T2.11) — reported and verified rather than fixed here, and still unfixed as of this fix round (2026-09-07: `src/components/buddy/state.ts:4` still reads `import { REFUSAL } from '@/lib/agents/buddy'`). Every budgetBytes value above already excludes this 375,465 bytes (i.e. assumes the fix lands), so perf:bundle fails on the current tree until it does; that failure is the gate correctly biting on a genuine, newly measured regression, not a bug in this script.

ledger.note: Fix-round addition (2026-09-07), found while adding these three routes' budget rows (see $routesAddedInFixRound above). All three now measure above their own v1 ceiling, which rule (a) forbids raising: /login 415,294 B vs a 346,112 B (338 KB v1) ceiling, +69,182 B; /admin 245,723 B vs a 203,776 B (199 KB v1) ceiling, +41,947 B; / 72,683 B vs a 71,680 B (70 KB v1) ceiling, +1,003 B. None of the three carries the buddy leak (confirmed: none of their manifests reference the leak chunk `415yhzio7b-ph.js`) or the Supabase pair except /login (see that row), so this weight is not explained by either row above. Root cause, read from src/app/layout.tsx and src/app/providers.tsx (both T0.6/T0.4 ownership, not T3.1's): `RootLayout` wraps every route, authenticated or not, in `<Providers>`, and `Providers` mounts `ThemeProvider` and `QueryProvider` and arms the sound manager unconditionally -- so /login, /admin and /, which had none of this in v1, now pay for all of it. This is architecture (every route gets consistent theming and a query client), not a bug, but it is also not one this task can accept or defer on another lane's behalf: flagging for T3.7 (the wave gate) to route to T0.4/T0.6 -- either these three routes are judged fine to carry this cost permanently (in which case a human ruling replaces this 'regression' status with 'accepted'), or a future task defers QueryProvider/the sound-manager arm off routes that render before authentication. Until that ruling lands, this status stays 'regression' rather than 'accepted' on purpose: nobody has actually decided this is fine yet, and marking it accepted would be this task deciding on their behalf.

Not part of the /exercise/[id] budget above at all — it never appears in entryJSFiles because Editor.tsx is next/dynamic({ ssr: false }) (spec §5.5), so it loads only once the editor mounts. Measured directly from the built react-loadable-manifest and per-language chunk fingerprints on this same tree, replacing the spec's '~400-500 KB, not measured' estimate: the always-loaded Editor bundle (basicSetup + @codemirror/state + @codemirror/view + Editor.tsx itself) is ~395 KB (404,666 bytes across its 4 chunk files, the `bytes` field above); the one grammar the exercise's language actually needs adds ~70 KB for Python (the lightest launch-course grammar, 71,808 bytes) up to ~139 KB for JavaScript/TypeScript/Mongo (142,317 bytes across 2 chunk files) or ~57 KB for SQL (58,788 bytes) on top of that — a single-grammar 'cold' editor load of roughly 465-535 KB, well under the audit's original monolithic all-five-grammars chunk (658 KB, shipped on every exercise regardless of language). `countedInBudget: false` because none of this — not even the 404,666-byte always-loaded base — is inside /exercise/[id]'s budgetBytes above; the CI printer renders this row as 'deferred, not in budget' rather than a byte figure, so it cannot be misread as 'CodeMirror costs ~0 KB'.

Not gated by this script — the gate above asserts tracked public/ only (git ls-files public), which never includes tools.jar (gitignored). tools.jar is fetched at build by `npm run prepare:java` and served same-origin, which the CheerpJ ruling (spec §3 C1) requires: Java is live (NEXT_PUBLIC_JUDGE_PROVIDER=browser), so a permanent 3 MB deploy cap and a shipped Java adapter cannot both be true. The plan's choice: keep tools.jar out of git and out of this gate, and carry its ~17.5 MB (measured: 18,361,919 bytes, sha256-verified at fetch time) as this named, permanent, accepted deploy-time cost instead of a CI assertion no build can pass while Java stays live. `routes: []` because this is a public/ deploy-time asset, not an app route -- it is exempt from the per-route ledger-coverage check by construction, not by omission.
